column8: What might help this person be more effective in the WHAT and/or the HOW? Provide 1-2 specific examples. Don't forget to consider the One ORBIT Autodesk Culture Guide
column9:
Simen could further increase his effectiveness by making his impact more visible, particularly in leadership and cross-org contexts—an opportunity aligned with Trust and Optimistic behaviors. He delivers significant value through foundational, behind-the-scenes work, but that impact isn’t always apparent unless someone is closely involved. More proactively sharing progress, outcomes, and wins would help others better understand and appreciate the value of the work.

Leaning slightly more into “selling” the work—through clear framing, storytelling, and positioning—would support his growth in a larger corporate environment. This doesn’t require changing how he works day-to-day, but rather amplifying the outcomes of that work for broader audiences. If he chooses to remain more IC-focused, his current approach is already highly effective; increasing visibility is simply a lever he can pull to expand influence and career optionality over time.

column8: The HOW: What behavior strengths did this person demonstrate consistently this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples. Don't forget to consider the One ORBIT Autodesk Culture Guide
column9:
Simen consistently demonstrates Trust, Relentless, and Ingenious behaviors. He is highly reliable and transparent, producing work that teams and leadership can depend on, which has significantly increased confidence in our data and decision-making. His ability to balance people leadership with hands-on execution builds strong trust across product, growth, and data teams.

He also shows a Relentless focus on outcomes, driving complex initiatives—such as instrumentation alignment and cross-org data unification—through ambiguity with persistence and accountability. At the same time, his Ingenious mindset is evident in how he reimagines data workflows, automates insights, and designs scalable foundations that enable experimentation and long-term growth.

column8: The WHAT: How has this individual made an impact and delivered results for your project/team/customers this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples.
column9:
Simen made a strong impact this year by establishing a durable data foundation and increasing data’s strategic influence across product and growth. He defined the data strategy and operating model, hired our first data engineer, and helped shape cross-team priorities—setting the conditions for clearer alignment and consistent delivery.

He significantly improved our data architecture and quality by delivering a redesigned schema and taxonomy, updating core definitions (retention, MAU), unifying Segment across Forma and ACS, and automating key insights—reducing manual effort and increasing trust in metrics.

Through close partnership with Growth, PMs, and leadership, Simen embedded data into decision-making via targeted deep dives and invested heavily in cross-org alignment, laying important groundwork for PLG and the Forma Industry Cloud.

column9: I work closely with Simen on a weekly and often daily basis. We partner across product analytics, deep-dive analyses, and business data to support decision-making, and collaborate closely on building the data infrastructure needed for product-led growth. Our work also involves regular cross-organization coordination to establish strong working relationships that enable future experimentation and measurement. Simen is a key partner in both day-to-day execution and longer-term strategic efforts.

column9: This feedback is more about Simen's team versus Simen himself, but I would like to see him find ways to encourage and facilitate proactive connection between his direct reports and peer data analysts and engineers in the company. I have not seen clear examples of Simen's strengths as a people manager yet, likely because our discussions so far have been focused on strategy, but he may have an opportunity to tactically grow his team's business knowledge and skillsets beyond the scope of his charter this upcoming year. He may want to consider identifying opportunities for joint projects, clarifying skill exchanges between teams, and creating structured collaboration (eg. having an IC level interlock periodically to exchange methods and ideas) to strengthen cross-team execution. This is something I personally aim to do with my team and plan to raise this with Simen as well.

column8: The HOW: What behavior strengths did this person demonstrate consistently this year? Provide 1-2 specific examples. Don't forget to consider the One ORBIT Autodesk Culture Guide
column9:
Simen consistently demonstrates our BRAVE value. Specifically, he “speaks up even when it’s unpopular or diverges from the status quo.” For example, when enterprise analytics tooling requirements posed high switching costs and end-user impact, he clearly articulated an alternative position and implemented an event-forwarding solution that met privacy and data-sharing requirements without requiring product teams to retool. His point of view is strong, yet fair and also sets a cultural precedence for other teams to seek impactful, pragmatic solutions. 


Simen also exemplifies and role models our ONE AUTODESK value. Specifically, he “create(s) success by collaborating across functions and teams—busting silos and sharing information and resources to achieve our goals and common purpose.” For example, he was able to facilitate and participate in seamless collaboration during our recent Forma data interlock to co-develop a joint point of view and future-state vision for Cloud Analytics at Autodesk. He is able to "see through the trees" and understands the big picture by putting impact and business use cases first. Without this open mindset and active listening in his leadership approach, the outcome could have resulted in reduced alignment between our teams, setting a precedent for a further disjointed business & data operations environment for our Cloud products.

Simen has provided thought leadership on optimizing data infrastructure for PLG applications, including guiding the retrofit of his team's analytics tooling (the WebSDK) and governance to meet enterprise requirements while minimizing switching costs. 


During the Forma Data Interlock in Dublin just this week, Simen helped define a shared vision for a best-in-class, outcomes-based Cloud Analytics infrastructure. This included a conceptual roadmap enabling cross-product and platform analytics and attribution for PLG applications, including ensuring PUPS compliance for Forma product usage collection.

1. Key impact on my learning. Simen has been a key partner in my learning while in a new role for several reasons. 1 - Did an amazing job responding to my request to create a development plan (optimistic). 2 - Has been very responsive to my request, feedback and sometimes difficult conversations (brave) to create an environment in which I am put in the best position to have learning opportunities by creating space for me to answer before he does, and by providing continuous feedback. 3 - Has been very responsive and patient (ONE Autodesk, trusted) with all my questions while learning both technical and soft skills, as well as the product.

3. Great manager. Based on the above, I also think that those attributes make him a fantastic manager because he encourages and supports ownership and autonomy, provides feedback, creates opportunities for learning and supports through challenges, thus delivering a results through his team.

2. Strategic thinking in the Growth org. Simen has very valuable contributions based on insights from the advanced analyses he is capable of doing, and based on his data science skills (relentless, ingenious). During the planning periods he contributes with key insights about user behaviour, and with strategic thinking for the direction to be set. During execution he contributes with valuable input to squads about experimentation, technical skills to create the insights automator, user behaviour insights and soft skills such as data storytelling, recommendations, stakeholder influence and management. I relied on him to manage situations I felt I needed help with.

Transparency and sharing
As mentioned, Simen is part of some highly strategic discussions and relevant initiatives that impact, for example, our content strategy. I believe there’s room for improvement in terms of sharing highlights from those interactions, so other stakeholders can plan and align accordingly. For example, takeaways from the gathering with the ACC data team.

Help drive tooling conversations and decisions
I think it’s been impactful that Simen took the lead on the Assistant scoping. I believe he is well positioned to lead some similar conversations about the future of Intercom, potential scope of XA insights etc, and we (data and content strategy) could be partners in this, rather than collaborate within specific initiatives. Currently these conversations are scattered across groups of stakeholders, but to progress us towards the Industry Cloud, it would be great with better defined ownership.

column9:
Simen consistently demonstrated the TRUSTED value through his effective leadership and commitment to team development.
Specific Example 1 (Onboarding): One thing I really appreciated was the highly patient and structured approach he took with my onboarding. He avoided overwhelming me with information, instead providing context and tasks bit by bit. By strategically connecting me with the right individuals and gradually increasing my responsibilities, he demonstrated genuine care and support, which built a foundation of trust and allowed me to quickly become self-sufficient.
Specific Example 2 (Delegation): He made a difference when he trusted the team's expertise by effectively delegating critical tasks and decisions. This action not only showcases his confidence in the team's capabilities but also allows us to move faster together and own our outcomes, making us more RELENTLESS in our execution.

column9:
Simen has made a significant impact by serving as the essential link between our team's daily execution and the broader corporate vision. He demonstrated the value of ONE AUTODESK by proactively collecting and synthesizing inputs from both our local product stakeholders and the global corporate strategy.
This effort resulted in a clear, actionable big-picture understanding of where the Data team needed to focus. By providing this strategic clarity, he ensured that our individual projects and tasks were perfectly aligned with the highest-priority corporate needs, maximizing our team's overall impact and benefits to the company.
